text: dsh-hint-shell 为 DeepSeek Harness 网页客户端的输入框添加 ! shell 前缀：用户在新消息开头输入 ! 和命令后，插件在会话工作目录运行命令，并把命令及输出记录为工具结果供下一次模型请求查看。空输入框会显示提示，单独输入 ! 时会提示如何继续；设置页可调整命令长度上限。它适合希望直接在 DSH 对话中运行 shell 命令并让后续对话引用结果的用户。使用时无需 API 密钥或额外账号。

dsh-hint-shell adds a ! prefix to the DSH web composer. Messages starting with ! plus a command run in the session directory; the command and output are saved as a tool result for the next turn. Hints explain the prefix; settings control its length limit. No API key or account is needed.
想在 DSH 输入框里直接运行 shell 命令，并让后续对话看到输出。
有没有办法用 !ls 这样的写法在当前会话目录执行命令？
让 DSH 空白输入框提示我可以用哪个符号运行终端命令。
我希望执行命令后把输出留在聊天记录里，下一轮还能引用。
How can I run a shell command from the DSH composer and keep its output in the conversation?
I want a visible composer hint when I type the shell prefix in DeepSeek Harness.
dsh-hint-shell 的功能「输入框 shell 提示」：在空输入框显示可用提示，用户只输入 ! 时在符号后显示引导文字；开始输入命令后提示消失。
dsh-hint-shell 的功能「执行命令并记录结果」：消息以 ! 和命令开头时，在会话工作目录运行 shell，并将命令、输出和状态写入会话工具记录。
dsh-hint-shell 的功能「设置命令长度上限」：插件设置页提供命令字符数上限；超长命令在启动子进程前拒绝，并将原因作为结果记录。

dsh-hint-shell README · dsh-hint-shell：> **🌐 Language** · [English](README.md) | [中文（简体）](README.zh.md)

Type `!` in the DeepSeek Harness composer and the rest of the line runs as a shell command, in the working directory of the session you are in.

It is the `!` of a terminal, moved into the chat box: no terminal window, no `bash` tool call of your own, and no model request spent on the command.

dsh-hint-shell README · Features：- **The composer tells you it is available.** An empty composer gains `, type ! for shell commands` after the shipped placeholder text, so `!` is discoverable without documenting it separately.
- **The hint appears as you type.** After a bare `!`, a gray `Enter a shell command…` appears right behind it, and the moment you type real text the hint disappears and gives the line back to you.
- **The output goes into the chat.** `!ls` returns its output as a tool call and result, so the next thing you ask the model about already includes it. **No model request is spent on the `!` line itself.**
- **Quoting, pipes, and globs behave as in a terminal.** The command runs through `/bin/sh -c`, or `cmd.exe` on Windows.
- **One setting.** The command length cap, on the plugin's own row under Installed.
- **Nothing else changes.** No new button, no replaced component, no altered keyboard behaviour.

dsh-hint-shell README · Installation：The repository ships **sources only**: `dist/` is git-ignored build output, so a Git checkout holds nothing the Harness can load. The installable artifact is the tarball attached to a GitHub Release, which is already built:

In the Plugin page, choose **Add plugin**, then paste the release asset address for the version you want:

```text
https://github.com/Mooling0602/dsh-hint-shell/releases/download/0.1.0/dsh-hint-shell-0.1.0.tgz
```

dsh-hint-shell README · Installation：A downloaded asset works the same way through its local path (`./dsh-hint-shell-<version>.tgz`). Restart DSH after it installs.

The same thing from the command line, for scripted setups:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add \
  https://github.com/Mooling0602/dsh-hint-shell/releases/download/0.1.0/dsh-hint-shell-0.1.0.tgz
```

A Git address also works, because `package.json` builds on install through its `prepare` script:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add github:Mooling0602/dsh-hint-shell
```

dsh-hint-shell README · Installation：That channel needs Node `^22.19.0 || >=24.0.0` and a build step, and pnpm blocks build scripts by default: allow the exact key pnpm prints in the profile's `pnpm-workspace.yaml` (`allowBuilds`) and re-run, or pass `--allow-build` for a one-off install.

dsh-hint-shell README · Installation：To update, repeat the installation with the new release asset. A tarball URL is pinned in the profile manifest, so moving between versions means `remove` and `add`. `dsh plugin` forwards to pnpm inside the profile directory, so never edit `~/.dsh/profiles/web/node_modules` by hand: the next pnpm operation overwrites it.

dsh-hint-shell README · Usage：1. Make sure the composer is empty.
2. Type `!` and keep typing the command, for example `!ls`, or `!git status`. The hint confirms that the `!` was recognised.
3. Press Enter.

The output is shown in the conversation, and the model can see the command and its result in the next request you send.

dsh-hint-shell README · When `!` is a shell prefix and when it is not：`!` is shell intent only when a command follows it on the same line, following the same rule the composer already applies to `/`:

| You type | What happens |
| --- | --- |
| `!ls` | Runs `ls`. |
| `! ls` | Runs `ls`. The space is ignored. |
| `!` alone | Ordinary text, sent to the model as prose. |
| `hello !world` | Ordinary text. A `!` in the middle of a sentence is not a trigger. |

A line that exceeds the command length cap is refused before it runs.
section: When `!` is a shell prefix and when it is not

text: dsh-hint-shell README · Limits：A `!` command obeys the same budget as the official `bash` tool, because it is transcribed into an ordinary tool call. The plugin reads that budget from the terminal plugin's own settings page at command time, so a timeout you tighten there applies to the next `!` command without a restart:

dsh-hint-shell README · Limits：| Field | Where it comes from |
| --- | --- |
| `timeoutMs` | the terminal plugin's page (`bash-sandbox`, or `pwsh-sandbox` on Windows) |
| `maxOutputBytes` | the same page |
| `maxCommandChars` | this plugin's own setting, default `10_000` characters |
| logged output | capped at `30_000` characters on the way into the session log |

dsh-hint-shell README · Limits：The length cap is the plugin's own because an ordinary tool call has none to inherit: the model writes the command into the request, so an unbounded line would be sent twice, once as the argument and once as the result's echo.

dsh-hint-shell README · What the model sees：A `!` result opens with this line:

```text
[run by the user via `!` prompt symbol]
```

The wire format does not carry who ran a command, so without it the model would read the record as a call it made itself. The line is a hint about provenance, not an isolation boundary; it tells the model what happened instead of leaving it to guess.

dsh-hint-shell README · Development：Sources are TypeScript; both shipped JavaScript files are generated.

```sh
npm install          # typescript + esbuild + @types/react + react
npm run typecheck    # tsc --noEmit
npm run build        # src/ -> dist/client.js, host.ts -> dist/index.js
npm test             # composer, shell-line, and installed-Harness format tests

dsh-hint-shell README · Development：`dist/` is not committed: the build writes only to that git-ignored directory, so a rebuild never dirties the tree. The shipped bundles come from the release tarball, which the release workflow packs from a fresh build of the tag.

`test/dsh-format.test.ts` drives the host hook against an installed Harness. It resolves the Harness packages from the host installation, and reports a skip when none is available.
dsh-hint-shell README · Implementation notes：The composer half reuses machinery the shipped composer already has, so the plugin adds no DOM, does no measurement, and does no positioning:

dsh-hint-shell README · Implementation notes：- **Idle hint.** `LocaleRuntime.prototype.translate` is wrapped, appending one clause to `conversation/placeholder.default` and `placeholder.hero`. Every other key passes through untouched, and uninstalling restores the original method.
- **Armed hint.** The shipped stylesheet already paints this kind of message through `--dsh-composer-hint`. Custom properties inherit, so setting that property on the composer card is enough for the existing rule to draw the text behind the typed `!`, in the shipped caption colour.
- **Draft reading.** The draft comes from `[data-composer-input]`, the editable surface the composer already publishes. Because Lexical commits typed text inside its own update pass, which is not guaranteed to finish before `input` fires, the plugin repaints on the mutation Lexical makes and keeps a deferred `input` read as a safety net.
- **Copy.** Strings live in the plugin's own `dsh-hint-shell` locale namespace, in `src/locales.ts`, in both languages. `locale/*.json` hold only `meta`, which the plugin listing reads through the Host.

dsh-hint-shell README · Implementation notes：The host half hooks `agent/pre-step`, the last point before the loop dispatches a request, and its `reject` decision is what makes a `!` line cost zero tokens. The outcome is recorded as a whole tool exchange rather than a single event, because a tool result with no preceding `tool-call` is a message answering a call that was never made, which a provider rejects. The records are written in the shape the session's format v4 reader validates on reopen; the live append would succeed even for a row that cannot be reopened, which is what the format test guards.

dsh-hint-shell README · Implementation notes：`subprocess` is read optionally rather than declared in `inject`, so the composer hints keep working even when no provider is composed; only execution degrades, and a `!` line then records a tool error naming the missing service.

dsh-hint-shell README · Layout：| Path | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `host.ts` | Host half: the `!` pre-step hook, record pair, and provenance line (source). |
| `dist/index.js` | Generated Host module, git-ignored. Do not edit. |
| `dist/client.js` | Generated Client bundle, git-ignored. Do not edit. |
| `build.mjs` | Bundles `src/` into `dist/`. |
| `PUBLISHING.md` | Release, install and update channels. |
| `src/config.ts` | The `Config` schema, and the limits read from the terminal entry. |
| `src/exec.ts` | Shell-line parsing, execution, and output formatting. |
| `src/locales.ts` | Every runtime string, in both languages. |
| `src/index.ts` | The composer effects: placeholder clause and hint painting. |
| `src/settings-page.tsx` | Registers the settings entry on the plugin's row. |
| `src/HintShellCard.tsx` | The settings form, and the row's one-line summary. |
| `src/hint-shell-card-controller.ts` | Staged-form controller over the config service. |
| `src/types.ts` | Structural types for the Client services used. |
| `src/host-types.ts` | Structural types for the Host services used. |
| `test/run.test.ts` | Composer integration test (fake DOM + fake locale). |
| `test/host.test

dsh-hint-shell README · Settings page placement：The entry is registered on `plugins.row.config`, keyed `dsh-hint-shell#dsh-hint-shell`, rather than on `plugins.item`. `plugins.item` *is* the Official group's slot, so registering there lists a third-party bundle's configuration among the built-in plugins; the row-config slot is the one meant for an installed package's own row.
